messages.subject: Re: package ‘seewave’ is not available (for R version 3.1.1)
messages.subject_clean: package ‘seewave’ is not available (for R version 3.1.1)
messages.body_plain:
Hi! Good morning!

I`m new in this forum and I just found it because I was looking for a way to install the "seewave" pkg on mac Yosemite. Well, after a long journey and visit diferent forums and blogs I got the solution and I would like to share, and if someone has the same problem can easily solved... =)

1st: If you do not have the R version 3.0.2 yet...install it first: you can find it on the old directories e.g. "http://stat.ethz.ch/CRAN/"

2nd: Make sure that you are using the 3.0.2 version. For that we have some options:

I) On the "Terminal" of your mac type: ls -l /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/
This will show you a list of version of R and also show which one is the current version.
II) you can also download the R switch here "http://r.research.att.com/" this will switch your R version, for one that you have installed (you can choose).

Ok. This step is easy. Now there is important steps that is nice do it before install all the pkg for seewave.

Go to the Terminal in your mac and type:

xcode-select --install

this will instal the xcode  (an integrated development environment).Agree with the license and then type on the terminal

make #and than hit enter

make install #and than hit enter

Now we are almost there, to get the seewave running...

But, first go to R and type:

install.packages(c("fftw","tuneR","rgl","rpanel"), repos="http://cran.at.r-project.org/") #this will install the pkgs
                                                                                                                                                                                                "fftw","tuneR","rgl","rpanel"

and finally:

install.packages("seewave", repos="http://cran.at.r-project.org/")

I think that this blog http://pblog.ebaker.me.uk/ can help if you have any doubt...at least help me a lot!

Now just have fun with seewave! =)

Kind regards,

Filipe

messages.subject: Method to count pulse rates?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm hoping you can help with a small question I have.  I'm new to R, so hopefully this isn't a silly question.  I'm analyzing frog calls, and I'm trying to incorporate some measure of individual pulses within calls.  It would be best if I could use a bit of code to do this automatically, as everything else is automatic (when my computer can handle it that is).

Any ideas on how to do this? I've attached an oscillogram of a single call to indicate what the pulses look like.  I can upload a .wav later if that helps too.

Thanks in advance!
Adam

PS. Many thanks to Jerome for a great package!

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Method to count pulse rates?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Adam,

What exactly do you need to know: just the time of each pulse/peak or its duration as well - the latter is more difficult, more so if starts and ends overlap.

For peak detection (thence timing) there is the package "Peaks" in R which includes Markov smoothing procedures. I may be wrong but I think the main smoothing obtained with the Hilbert transform is just because a window of n samples is used for the transform. From your spectrogram, Markov smoothing over a much shorter window (n < 10) could be simpler and with higher precision,

For determining the beginning and ends (peak width), I was unsuccessful when looking for suitable existing code (R or C++) for noisy data and had to set about it myself (work in progress - sorry!). The simplest, which may be all you need, would be measures of when each pulse passes above/below a given faction of the peak height.I don't know of a package for doing that though.

Krzysz

messages.subject: Re: Method to count pulse rates?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Adam,
I needed to do the same (or something similar): to detect chirps (or pulses) in a particular frequency band. First I filtered the signal to get rid of any extraneous disturbing frequencies, then I ran the following function, adapted from the peaks function:

> amppeaks=function(wave, f, threshold=1.2, plot = TRUE
>                   , smooth = 3000, col = 2, cex = 1, symbol = ".",clip.value=7.5,...)
> {
>   input <- inputw(wave = wave, f = f)
>   f <- input$f
>   smoothenv <- env(input$w,ssmooth=smooth,f,plot=F)
>   rm(input)
>   loc.max <- which(smoothenv > threshold*mean(smoothenv))
>   amp <- smoothenv[loc.max]
>   if (is.na <http://is.na>(mean(amp))) {clipped=0;amp=0;loc.max=0} else if (mean(amp)<clip.value) {clipped=0} else {clipped=1}
>   if (plot) {
>     plot(smoothenv~c(1:length(smoothenv)/f), type="h",ylab="amplitude",xlab="time (seconds)")
>     text(x = loc.max/f, y = max(smoothenv), labels = symbol, cex = cex, col = col)
>   }
>   return(data.frame(val = amp, loc = (loc.max/f), clipped = clipped))
> }

For the moment the parameters (threshold and smooth) are tuned to my specific problem, but I believe it will work well for your problem too. I rarely had to correct manually. It also detects whether the signal is clipped (clip.value=7.5 worked in my case).
Actually I sent this function to Jérôme but he said a better one written by one of his students would be included later in Seewave.
Best,
Kevin

messages.subject: pulse function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I tried to run the example of the pulse function but it produces an error:

pulse(dbefore=0.5,dpulse=0.1,dafter=0.3,f=44100,plot=F)
  argument "freq" is missing, with no default

when I replace the argument "f" by "freq" I got this:

pulse(dbefore=0.5,dpulse=0.1,dafter=0.3,freq=44100,plot=F)

Error in initialize(value, ...) :
  invalid names for slots of class “Wave”: dbefore, dpulse, dafter, plot

I was just exploring the function, but it seems that there is an internal inconsistency in the function

Cheers

Marcelo Araya-Salas
Ph.D. Candidate
Wright Behavior Lab
Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Program
New Mexico State University
